newsitem.title: USA: IBM works with insurers on Internet risks.
newsitem.headline: IBM works with insurers on Internet risks.

text.p: International Business Machines Corp said it is working with three insurers to design new products and services that will protect businesses from Internet-related liabilities.

IBM, which made the announcement Monday as the 35th annual Risk and Insurance Management Society conference got underway here, said it will work with Chubb Corp, Reliance National and Danish insurer Codan to cover these new and growing cyberspace risks.
Jay Brown, claims counsel for Employers Casualty Co, a unit of General Electric Co's Employers Re Corp in Overland Park, Kansas, provided several examples where there might be gaps in coverage.
For instance, he said a travel agency sponsored a forum for travelers to share experiences. One of the participants complained about a resort and the "stoned" scuba instructor.
The resort filed a defamation suit against both the party making the statement and the travel agency, Brown said.
In another case, a manufacturer was sued for copyright infringement because its Web site contained another company's advertisement, which used unauthorized video and music clips, he said.
In its statement, IBM said it intends to use its experience in Internet security to help bring clarity and understanding to Internet exposures and help control losses.
The planned products and services, IBM said, are logical extensions of insurers' traditional product lines.
"Businesses are putting their assets online and facing growing electronic exposures," IBM global insurance industry general manager Fred Amoroso said in a statement.
IBM said it believes that insurers that build Internet insurance into their services now will benefit the most from this growing and largely untapped market.
Chubb technology insurance group vice president Thomas Cornwell said the Internet calls for new insurance approaches.
"In today's new global electronic business arena, yesterday's loss prevention approaches and insurance responses simply no longer fit," Cornwell said.

"Companies that regard their current liability insurance portfolio as a safety net for their Internet activities may be in for an unfortunate surprise should they have a loss in cyberspace," he said in a statement.
Reliance National executive vice president of marketing Mark Owens said he believes the threat to businesses is real.
"The threat caused by hackers today is real and businesses operating online need to be aware that they are exposed," he said.
Indeed, the Internet is a hot topic at this year's RIMS conference, where at least five separate seminars are scheduled to discuss potential cyberspace liability.
At one session late Monday afternoon, the speakers warned risk managers that their traditional commercial general liability policies may not cover them for all of their Internet- related risks.
